jobs.description: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. As a Staff SSD Validation Engineer at Micron Technology, Inc., you will be responsible for defining and driving comprehensive validation strategies for Micron NAND-based SSD systems and solutions. You will lead development of test plans, test cases, and automation frameworks to validate SSD firmware across functional, system-level, performance, reliability, interoperability, and customer qualification domains. You will serve as a technical leader, driving validation excellence, automation, and innovation while collaborating closely with firmware, hardware, systems, product engineering, and hyperscale customers throughout the product lifecycle. The ideal candidate will possess deep expertise in NVMe/PCIe technologies, SSD architecture, customer qualification requirements, and automated validation methodologies. This role also requires a strong focus on leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) and advanced automation technologies to improve validation productivity, product quality, and time-to-market. Key Responsibilities Define validation strategies, test plans, test cases, and automation frameworks for SSD firmware validation. Develop and maintain automated test solutions covering functional, system, performance, reliability, interoperability, and customer qualification requirements. Lead validation efforts across all phases of the product lifecycle, including development, qualification, customer enablement, and sustaining activities. Demonstrate strong understanding of NVMe, PCIe, OCP Cloud SSD specifications, storage protocols, and customer-specific requirements. Partner with Micron's hyperscale and datacenter customers to improve product quality, customer satisfaction, and qualification cycle times. Drive issue identification, debug, root cause analysis, and closure through effective collaboration with firmware, hardware, system architecture, and product engineering teams. Analyze validation results, identify quality risks, and provide clear recommendations to stakeholders and leadership. Communicate validation status, technical risks, mitigation plans, and project progress effectively across organizations. Influence and lead cross-functional teams to execute validation strategies and achieve program milestones. Operate effectively in ambiguous environments and independently drive high-impact initiatives to completion. Mentor engineers and promote technical excellence, automation, and best practices across the validation organization. Leverage AI-powered engineering tools and approved enterprise AI solutions to improve test development, debug efficiency, data analysis, and reporting workflows. Identify opportunities to apply AI and machine learning techniques for automating validation workflows, failure analysis, anomaly detection, and predictive quality analytics. Drive adoption of AI-enabled solutions to reduce manual effort, enhance test coverage, accelerate issue triage, and improve validation throughput. Utilize Generative AI tools for code generation, test case development, log analysis, technical documentation, and productivity enhancement while adhering to company policies. Champion responsible and ethical AI practices, ensuring compliance with Micron AI governance, security, privacy, and data protection requirements. Mentor teams on effective AI adoption, prompt engineering techniques, and AI-assisted engineering workflows to improve organizational productivity and innovation. Strong understanding of SSD architecture, NAND Flash technologies, and storage subsystems. Deep knowledge of NVMe, PCIe, OCP Cloud SSD, and enterprise storage specifications. Experience with Datacenter Compute and Storage environments such as Microsoft Hyper-V, VMware vSphere, VSAN, and cloud infrastructure is a strong plus. Strong hands-on experience debugging NVMe/SAS protocol issues using protocol analyzers such as LeCroy and JDSU. Experience developing comprehensive validation plans involving I/O workloads, NVMe protocols, media management, endurance, and reliability testing. Experience using storage validation platforms and tools such as Medusa, SanBlaze, OakGate, UNH, PCIe-CV, and related qualification suites. Experience integrating tests into automated validation frameworks and continuous integration environments. Proven ability to drive complex technical issues to closure across multiple organizations. Experience reviewing, analyzing, tracking, and documenting validation results and product quality issues. Demonstrated leadership in driving validation strategies for large-scale programs and customer engagements. Successful Candidates Will Have Technical Skills Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field. Strong programming expertise in Python and test automation framework development. Strong Linux and Windows debugging experience. Excellent knowledge of storage systems and platform architecture, including CPU, Memory, PCIe, Drivers, Operating Systems, Firmware, and Hardware interactions. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills. Experience with large-scale automation environments and continuous validation systems. Ability to analyze complex technical data and make informed engineering decisions. AI & Data-Driven Engineering Skills Demonstrated proficiency in leveraging AI tools to improve engineering productivity and technical decision-making. Understanding of Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), prompt engineering, and practical AI use cases within engineering workflows. Experience using AI-assisted development tools for scripting, debugging, test generation, report creation, and knowledge discovery. Knowledge of machine learning fundamentals, data analytics, and AI-enabled automation techniques is highly desirable. Ability to critically review and validate AI-generated outputs and apply engineering judgment to ensure technical accuracy. Commitment to responsible AI usage, data governance, security, privacy, and ethical AI practices. Leadership & Professional Skills Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Strong project planning, execution, and organizational skills. Ability to lead multiple priorities and programs simultaneously. Ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct authority. Results-oriented mindset with the ability to drive execution in fast-paced and ambiguous environments. Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic is seeking an exceptional Legal Program Manager to serve as the operational backbone of contracting for the Compute and Infrastructure team. We'll rely on you to manage a high volume of procurement and vendor agreements — including datacenter colocation, lease, and build-to-suit agreements; hardware, chip, and network-equipment procurement; and construction, facilities, and operations-and-maintenance (O&M) contracts — along with the NDAs, order forms, SOWs, and amendments that surround them. You will build the scalable contracting processes — templates, playbooks, intake and approval workflows, and contract lifecycle management — that let the business move at the speed of Anthropic’s infrastructure buildout. This role owns the system, throughput, and visibility that move every agreement from intake through signature.
Key responsibilities
Coordinate and shepherd a high volume of compute and infrastructure procurement transactions — datacenter colocation, lease, and build-to-suit agreements; hardware, chip, and network-equipment procurement; construction/EPC and facilities/O&M agreements; and the supporting NDAs, order forms, SOWs, and amendments — driving each from intake through signature
Own and administer the contract lifecycle management system: workflow design and configuration, templates, approval routing, signing and archive and integrity hygiene
Design and run intake and triage: how requests enter, how they are prioritized, and how they route to the right owner
Propose and develop scalable solutions to improve contracting efficiency and throughput across the infrastructure vendor base
Collaborate with business units and legal team members to streamline contract management processes, manage post-signature obligations and renewals across the infrastructure vendor portfolio, identify potential risks, and drive continuous improvement in contract handling efficiency
Partner closely with the Compute and Infrastructure, Product, Finance, Security, Business Operations, and Procurement Ops teams to achieve key business objectives and deliver strategic, business-minded, and solutions-focused counsel
Build reporting, dashboards, SLAs, and the metrics that surface turnaround times and bottlenecks across the infrastructure vendor portfolio
Deploy LLM and AI tooling to scale contracting throughput and reduce manual handling
Minimum Qualifications
Experience operating in a fast-paced technology startup in which priorities shift rapidly and schedules "move to the left," thriving in this dynamic environment and priding yourself on your adaptability and ability to pivot with speed and grace
Initiative and autonomy in managing complex contractual matters, effectively prioritizing competing deadlines
An understanding of what's important in the context of a contract, the organization's mission, and enough contract fluency to triage and route requests, track obligations, and pull in relevant legal counsel
Excitement to grow with an organization and help shape the culture of the commercial function
A preference for straightforward, concise explanations over legalese and overwrought drafting
A knack for identifying and implementing efficient processes and policies
The ability to thrive as a member of cross-functional teams building frontier technologies, with a desire to develop a deep understanding of the Compute & Infrastructure teams and the datacenter, hardware, and network systems they build and operate
Comfort operating outside your areas of expertise and in uncharted legal territory
A "doer" mentality, willing to roll up your sleeves to get things done as a team player who doesn't hesitate to jump in to do work that needs to get done, whether glamorous or not
Hands-on experience with contract lifecycle management or legal-operations tooling, process design, and working from data, metrics, and dashboards
Comfort using AI and LLM tools to streamline and scale routine contracting work
Preferred Qualifications
10+ years in contract management, legal operations, or procurement operations, including hands-on experience implementing or administering a contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform; experience supporting infrastructure, datacenter, hardware, construction, or telecom/network procurement and vendor contracting
Proven ability to collaborate across various organizational levels and functions to facilitate efficient contracting processes and execution while building strong relationships

Excellent verbal and written communication, analytical, collaboration, and interpersonal skills

Experience implementing or administering a CLM platform (Ironclad) and standing up reporting and metrics

Position Summary Join a team at the heart of grid reliability and customer impact, where your decisions help restore power and keep communities running. The Distribution Control Center (DCC) is the hub that monitors and controls the electric distribution system, coordinates switching and restoration activities, as well as completes device commissioning and modeling to safely and reliably serve customers. In this critical, fast-paced role, you will play a key part in restoring power and supporting grid reliability by monitoring, analyzing, and managing outage events across Duke Energy’s distribution system. You will evaluate outage data, coordinate and direct field resources, and ensure accurate, real-time information is captured to support efficient restoration efforts at the feeder level and below. Working closely with the technical Grid Management team, Senior DCC Operators, and DCC Operations leadership, you will also assist in substation restoration as needed. You will be responsible for modeling work within OMS, DMS, and/or SCADA systems, and controlling the Distribution grid. A critical responsibility as the grid Control Authority includes the issuance of safety and operational tags such as HLTs, Clearance, Do Not Operate, and Information Tags. All switching and tagging activities under the distribution control authority will be fully managed by this role, to ensure safe and efficient response to planned and emergent work impacting the distribution grid. Successful candidates will thrive in high-pressure environments and are energized by problem-solving during critical events. You will play a vital role during abnormal conditions and large-scale outages, providing essential support and contributing to emergency and storm response operations. This role serves as vital support during abnormal or emergency events, requiring sound judgment and the ability to perform under pressure. This opportunity offers exposure to complex grid operations in a 24/7 environment, with rotational shifts and on-call responsibilities that directly support service reliability when it matters most. To be considered for this role, candidates must successfully pass the System Operator/Power Dispatching (SOPD) II test. Once selected for this role, all Operator I positions must successfully pass the Operator Training Certification program and progress to Operator II. The Operator Training Certification program typically takes eighteen to twenty-four months and consists of classroom instruction, on-the-job (OJT) training, and simulator training and assessments. Responsibilities Direct outage dispatching for feeder level outages and below and assist with substation outages. Review outage information and dispatch appropriate field resources to restore power, troubleshoots and analyzes problems to provide possible fault locations and direct restoration efforts. Review, update and ensure correct outage information is modeled in the Outage Management System (OMS) and Distribution Management System (DMS). Also, ensure that the Distribution System model is kept accurate in OMS and DMS to ensure the best optimization. Authorize, record and model in the OMS and DMS: Hot Line Tags (HLT), Clearance tags, Do Not Operate (DNO) tags, and Information tags. Under supervision and direction of Supervisor, Sr DCC Operator, or designee directs and models switching activities in order to maintain an accurate distribution model of the system for the best optimization for megawatts (MWs) from DMS. Periodically review tags in the system to ensure tags are removed promptly and that the system model and data are accurate. Monitor SCADA and DMS systems including remotely opening and closing Feeder Circuit Breakers, Reclosers, and Regulators under normal and emergency situations. Install and remove HLTs remotely. Monitor alarms from SCADA and DMS and assist with determining appropriate response (e.g. low/high voltages, transformer load/temperature alarms, abnormal feeder lockouts, etc.) and provide notification/reports to others. Assist in directing restoration efforts associated with large outages (e.g. feeder lockouts, substation outages, transmission line interruptions, etc.) and ensure that the OMS and DMS models are kept accurate for distribution system optimization to achieve MW reductions if called for on the Distribution System. jobs.description:
About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic is hiring a Field Marketing Lead dedicated to the Public Sector Industry — one of the fastest-growing customer segments we serve, and one we believe will define how the next generation of AI-native companies adopts and builds with Claude. You will own the field marketing strategy and end-to-end execution for Public Sector audiences in the US, partnering closely with our Public Sector Sales teams.
This is a builder role. Field Marketing at Anthropic is a small, scrappy team and the Public Sector is an area of growth for the business — there is no existing playbook for you to inherit. You will design the event calendar, build the integrated digital programs, develop the necessary partnerships, and create the playbooks that scale across our Public Sector motion.
Responsibilities
Develop and activate the US Public Sector field marketing strategy end-to-end — planning, calendar, execution, and measurement.
Design and run public-sector-appropriate event formats — agency roundtables, mission-focused briefings, tech demo days, industry days, and executive breakfasts — that comply with government ethics and gift rules while building trusted relationships with program and procurement stakeholders
Plan the field calendar around the government fiscal year — building demand programs that peak ahead of federal year-end (September 30) and state budget cycles, and capitalize on use-it-or-lose-it spending windows
Own presence at anchor public sector events — from sponsorship strategy to speaker placement and on-site execution
Build co-marketing programs with the public sector channel ecosystem — distributors, resellers, systems integrators, and contract-vehicle holders — including joint events, teaming-oriented content, and partner-sourced pipeline
Partner closely with Public Sector Sales and BDRs on pre-event targeting, during-event engagement, and post-event follow-up to convert attention into pipeline
Build operational playbooks (Demo Day activation kit, hackathon kit) that the Field Marketing team can scale across regions and segments
Establish baseline metrics, dashboards, and ROI reporting for all Public Sector field programs
Be the face of Anthropic in the Public Sector ecosystem — credible with strategic partners and agencies
Minimum qualifications
Direct Public Sector-segment experience — you have built and run programs targeting the Public Sector as your primary audience, not as an enterprise field marketer who occasionally touches Public Sector
End-to-end ownership of field marketing events and programs, hands on in both strategy and execution - this is a 0-1 building role with very little foundation in place
Repeat success across multiple companies — we are looking for a pattern of impact, scaling field or demand generation programs in different environments, not a single-company tour (however strong the brand)
0-to-1 builder DNA — you've built a field marketing motion from scratch (or rebuilt one), and you also have scaled-company tenure that grounds you operationally
Tight sales alignment — you've worked shoulder-to-shoulder with AEs and BDRs on account targeting, pre-event outreach, and post-event follow-up
Operational rigor — you can stand up vendor management, registration, follow-up workflows, and ROI dashboards without being asked
Technical credibility — you can review technical event content, brief technical speakers, and hold your own with founder/CTO audiences
Preferred qualifications
10+ years across Field Marketing, Demand Generation, ABM, and Events at B2B technology companies
Experience working inside of a Public Sector organization that went through a rapid growth phase, or a blend of Public Sectors and scaled technology companies.
AI/ML field marketing experience
Existing relationships with public sector associations and research institutions
Visible thought leadership in the Public Sector ecosystem or developer ecosystem
Role-specific policy:
For this role, we expect staff to be able to work from our San Francisco or Washington, D.C. office at least 2 days a week. We encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time for relocation.
The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.
For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit
anthropic.com/careers
directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.

jobs.description: About Us Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid. At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world. Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you. Job Description The Global Data Office As artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies become increasingly central to Visa’s innovation agenda, the Global Data Office (GDO) is expanding its AI and Data Governance function to ensure responsible, compliant, and effective use of these capabilities across the enterprise. In this role, you will drive Visa’s Responsible Data Use program – evaluating cutting-edge AI and data initiatives – to safeguard trust and unlock business value. You will be at the forefront of Visa’s innovation, guiding how new AI solutions roll out globally while ensuring they meet our obligations to clients, regulators, and consumers. This position offers a unique opportunity to lead cross-functional collaborations, take ownership of mission-critical processes, and shape policies that govern data and AI use at Visa. Key Responsibilities Drive and enhance the Data & AI Use Case Assessment process – a key engine of Visa’s innovation – enabling calculated, transparent risk-taking for faster business growth. You will continuously improve this process to support new AI/data initiatives while maintaining compliance and trust. Execute a wide range of initiatives to implement Visa’s Responsible Data Use framework, including spearheading organizational change management efforts that embed data ethics into the company’s culture. Collaborate across all Visa regions and functions as a catalyst in Visa’s innovation pipeline. Work cross-functionally with teams (Product, Innovation, Analytics, Privacy, etc.) to operationalize data use guidelines globally, ensuring every project meets our standards and obligations. Conduct thorough Data & AI use case reviews: Examine incoming data use requests in detail and evaluate their risk against established Data & AI policies and rules. Where necessary, dive deep into technical specifics (even reverse-engineering algorithms) to ensure compliance and effectiveness. Lead end-to-end analysis of use cases: Take charge of reviews for complex AI and data projects. Identify and document potential risks with precision, bring in additional subject-matter experts for insight when needed, and synthesize all feedback into clear, actionable review reports. Take ownership of expert consultations: Engage internal subject-matter experts (legal, compliance, technology, etc.) to gather feedback on data use scenarios that fall outside existing guidelines. You’ll own these collaborations, ensuring that no critical insight is missed when assessing novel or ambiguous cases. Drive policy improvements: Proactively identify gaps or gray areas in current data use policies. Coordinate with internal stakeholders to propose well-founded policy updates or alternative solutions, backing your recommendations with solid facts and analysis to drive leadership discussions. Provide thought leadership in Data & AI: Develop and share informed perspectives on emerging data and AI domains, including responsible AI, generative AI, data governance, privacy-enhancing technologies, and evolving regulatory expectations. Translate external developments and review insights into practical guidance that shapes policy, strategy, and decision-making across Visa. Champion training and awareness: Help lead workshops and training sessions that educate Visa staff on our Data Use Policy and core data values. Be prepared to step up and lead training sessions, inspiring teams across the organization to uphold responsible data practices. Mentor and develop junior colleagues: Provide day-to-day coaching, constructive feedback, and practical guidance to junior team members. Support their development of sound judgement, technical and policy expertise, and confidence in leading complex Data & AI use case reviews and stakeholder engagements. Amplify our Data & AI Policy & Governance message: Create and curate engaging content for the Global Data Office’s internal sites and our external “Data @ Visa” pages. Your content will showcase progress, highlight success stories, and reinforce the importance of responsible AI and data use. Communicate progress and insights: Prepare compelling materials (presentations, reports, dashboards) to socialize Data & AI Use Policy developments and share insights from Data Use Case Assessment reviews with stakeholders at all levels. Ensure transparency, buy-in, and alignment on data governance initiatives. Take on new challenges: Support ad-hoc Data Policy projects and new initiatives as they arise. Whether it’s a sudden regulatory change or a novel business proposal, you are ready to jump in, adapt, and contribute to solutions in real time. Connect policy and practice: Make sure learnings from Data & AI use case reviews inform the broader data governance strategy. Share insights across teams (“cross-pollination”) so that our policies, guidelines, and operations all advance together in a unified, informed way. Partner with data stakeholders: Work closely with Data Stewards and data requestors to gather complete and detailed information for each use case upfront. By ensuring you have all the facts, you enable more efficient reviews and more effective risk assessments. Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager. Qualifications Basic Qualifications 8 or more years of relevant work experience with a Bachelor Degree or at least 5 years of experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or 2 years of work experience with a PhD Preferred Qualifications 9 or more years of relevant work experience with a Bachelor Degree or 7 or more relevant years of experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or 3 or more years of experience with a PhD Proven experience in data and AI domains: Solid background in data science, data governance, data privacy, or a related field. (Experience in the payments or fintech industry is a plus.) Deep understanding of AI/ML technologies: Familiarity with cutting-edge techniques – particularly generative AI and large language models (LLMs) – and a strong awareness of ethical AI and responsible data use frameworks. Technical proficiency: Hands-on skills in quantitative analysis and data tooling (e.g. statistics, coding, or data engineering). While not expected to apply these skills directly, you should be comfortable interpreting complex datasets and algorithms to evaluate complex datasets or algorithms, and you grasp how to apply mathematics and statistics in assessing policy compliance. Knowledge of data regulations: Familiarity with evolving data and AI legislation (e.g., EU AI Act, GDPR, CCPA) and the ability to incorporate regulatory requirements into your assessments and recommendations. Exceptional problem-solving abilities: Creative, out-of-the-box thinking to tackle complex data challenges. You find solutions that satisfy policy objectives while enabling business innovation. Track record of results: A history of delivering high-impact projects in fast-paced, high-volume environments. You meet ambitious goals and can handle multiple priorities without sacrificing quality. Strong communication & stakeholder management: Excellent interpersonal skills with a proactive communication style. You’re able to engage and influence cross-functional teams – from engineers to lawyers to business leaders – ensuring everyone understands and aligns with data policy objectives. Clarity in complexity: Ability to interpret complex technical documents (policies, standards, procedures) and distill them into clear, concise guidance for non-technical audiences. You can translate “legal/technical speak” into actionable business terms that others readily grasp. Thrives under pressure: Energized by challenges, you excel in high-pressure, high-volume settings – delivering quality results even when working with demanding stakeholders and tight deadlines. Team leadership and collaboration: A true team player who is highly collaborative and diplomatic. You build strong relationships across diverse teams and lead by example, fostering an environment of trust and high performance. Meticulous and quality-focused: Keep attention to detail in everything you do, while still keeping sight of the bigger picture. You take pride in producing work that is accurate and of high quality. Exceptional problem solver: Superior analytical thinking with demonstrated intellectual rigor. When faced with a complex or ambiguous problem, you approach it systematically and resourcefully, finding innovative solutions. Self-motivated with ownership mentality: An independent self-starter who takes full ownership of your responsibilities. You have a strong sense of accountability for your deliverables and drive initiatives forward with minimal oversight. Adaptable and flexible: Comfortable working in a fast-changing, often ambiguous environment. You adapt quickly to new information and changing circumstances, staying effective and positive amid uncertainty. Open and innovative mindset: Open-minded and receptive to feedback and new ideas. You actively listen to others’ perspectives and are willing to change approach when current processes aren’t sufficient, always seeking better solutions. Enthusiastic & results-driven: Bring a high level of enthusiasm to your work and maintain an unrelenting focus on results. You’re driven to exceed targets and set new standards, motivated by the impact you create. Global mindset: Excited to work in a multicultural, global environment. You value diverse perspectives and are respectful and mindful of cultural differences when collaborating with colleagues around the world. Information for US Applicants For roles located in the US, the estimated salary range for this position is $180,600.00 to $ 289,300.00 USD per year, which may include potential sales incentive payments (if applicable). Salary may vary depending on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location.
